newsitem.title: USA: Woman question's caretaker's Cunanan claim.
newsitem.headline: Woman question's caretaker's Cunanan claim.

text.p: A woman told police she saw a caretaker enter a Miami Beach houseboat two days before suspected killer Andrew Cunanan committed suicide there, contradicting his account of events, media reports said on Tuesday.
The caretaker, Fernando Carreira, is demanding the $45,000 reward for leading detectives to Cunanan, who is believed to have killed fashion designer Gianni Versace on July 15.
Carreira called police last Wednesday after he spotted a pair of sandals, a blanket and a pillow on the boat and then heard a shot. After storming the houseboat, police found Cunanan's body.

Carreira said he had not checked the boat for five days previously. But the Miami Herald and local radio reported that a 71-year-old woman named Lola Dudley told police on Monday she saw the caretaker enter the boathouse two days before the suicide, carrying a lunchbox and a gallon of milk.
"I believe our detectives spoke to her. I can't get into the validity of her story at this point," Miami Beach police spokesman Bernie Ruder told Reuters.
FBI spokesman Anne Figueiras said the agency would like to speak to her. "She says she saw him go in the houseboat and a different time to what he says. We'll see if that checks out," she said.
Dudley reportedly said she was changing buses when she saw Carreira.

Police and city officials have so far declined to give Carreira the reward money. He has hired a lawyer and has been appeared on nationwide television since his role in the saga's finale emerged. On Monday he was feted by a gay and lesbian group in New York that handed him a check for $10,000.
